That low entry is also the cause of the pour stage's compile error: its path z band [+0.080,+0.100] m is 0.07 m away from the entry. Rewrite the pour stage after the transport height is fixed, and note that its path rotation row (front_axis antiparallel mug.up, tight) is also unsatisfiable at entry, since the pot arrives upright — the path must permit the tilt to progress while keeping the spout over the opening and above the rim.

rounds.diagnosis: The pour path lets the spout tip wander up to ±5 cm laterally from mug.opening_center and anywhere from 8 to 20 cm above the rim while the roll (the tilt that starts the flow) is free. Tea begins leaving the spout partway through the tilt, so poses allowed by these loose terms would pour outside the mug or drop the stream from an excessive height. Narrow the path's centering term to moderate and the above-clearance slack to moderate so the spout stays over the mug mouth and at a sane pouring height throughout the tilt; the subgoal and the transport stage are otherwise sound.

rounds.diagnosis: Everything about the transport stage is sound (upright enforced tight along the whole path, spout centred over the mug at a real standoff, the nominal-pose graze of the mug is a planner concern). The pour stage's only weakness is aim: the spout tip is held 8-13 cm above the rim and may be 2 cm off-centre, while the spout direction is only required to be within 15 deg of straight down. At that pour height a 15 deg tilt error plus the lateral offset can put the stream ~5 cm from the mug axis, outside the opening. Tightening the spout-down row to tight keeps the aim error under ~1 cm of drift so the tea lands in the mug for every pose the region allows.
